habits that make you
impossible to intimidate

calm disagreement

once a week, calmly and kindly disagree out loud with something you don't believe. people respect a clear opinion far more than polite silence and nodding.

asking what they meant

when a comment stings, ask what did you mean by that, in a calm voice. most little digs fall apart the moment you ask someone to explain them clearly.

learning how people work

spend 5 minutes a day on one idea from psychology: why we people please, how habits form. understanding how people work makes them far less intimidating.

slides.texte_overlay:
writing your first line

before a hard conversation, write the one sentence you need to say on paper. walking in with a clear first line keeps your voice steady when nerves kick in.

no over explaining

when you say no, give one reason or none at all, never five. over explaining sounds like asking for permission, while a short answer sounds sure of itself.
